page: OVHcloud r2-120 is a memory-optimized server instance virtualized via KVM. It features an Intel x86_64 processor based on the Haswell architecture without TSX, operating at a clock speed of 2.2 GHz. The configuration provides 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs, meaning hyperthreading is disabled with exactly 1.0 thread per core. It is equipped with 120.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 15.0 GB per core. Storage is provided by a local 200 GB SSD, and network connectivity is rated at a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear tradeoff between compute power and memory capacity. Single-core CPU performance is in the bottom 10% according to stress-ng, and multi-core performance is weak, ranking in the bottom 25%. However, memory-centric benchmarks show better results; cached small-block read bandwidth, Passmark memory scores, and Passmark database operations all rank in the average tier. Redis SET operations also perform at an average level, processing 8.58 million operations per second. Conversely, uncached large-block memory write bandwidth is poor, falling into the bottom 10%.

Given its high memory density relative to its compute capabilities, the r2-120 offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive, modern CPU instructions. It is well-suited for in-memory caching, database operations, and software compilation, where its average Geekbench clang compilation and Passmark database scores align with resource availability. It is less suitable for CPU-heavy tasks like large-scale LLM inference, where text generation speeds for a 7B model fall into the poor category at 4.93 tokens per second, or high-throughput static web serving.
